source.title: Symmetric Cross Entropy for Robust Learning With Noisy Labels
source.authors: Yisen Wang; Xingjun Ma; Zai-Yi Chen; Yuan Luo; Jin-Feng Yi; James Bailey

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how test accuracy changes across label-noise rates, using a noisy-label experiment rather than random-label fitting as in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracy under multiple label-noise rates. It does not report training error for these runs. Its discussion of earlier memorization findings cites other work and is not extracted as a result.
record.test_reason: The standard-CE experiments use SGD training and test accuracy across random-label corruption rates, directly testing V4's degradation component. They do not establish perfect training fit or the order of learning clean and noisy labels.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors identify hard-class underlearning alongside noisy-label overfitting under CE, and conclude that their symmetric cross-entropy approach addresses both and improves robustness.
record.recipe_differences: The paper varies symmetric label-noise rates and reports test accuracy; it does not use completely random labels or measure their training fit.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, loss, and label-noise rate vary across the reported experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 3.2 and Figures 1–4 show class-dependent learning: hard classes remain poorly learned while easy-class test accuracy drops later in training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under label noise, standard cross-entropy learning can combine persistent hard-class underlearning with easy-class overfitting.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision
record.problems: For the claim versions, the relevant results report test accuracy only; they do not report training error or establish zero training error at any noise rate. The table is flattened in the supplied text, though its headings and row order support these CIFAR-10 CE assignments.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 reports additional methods, datasets, and asymmetric-noise conditions. They were omitted because they do not add rows for the tested V4 condition group selected here. Figures 1–9 also include results about the proposed SL method, class-wise accuracy, parameter analysis, and ablations; they do not measure the claim's training-fit outcome.

untested.parts: Near-zero training error on completely random labels, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training time relative to true labels and convergence speed across corruption fractions.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian inputs.
Perfect training fit throughout the sweep, complete corruption, and the chance-performance endpoint; simultaneous signal learning and noise memorization are not directly measured.
Whether explicit regularizers prevent random-label fitting and whether removing them impairs clean-label generalization.
Direct comparison of clean-pattern learning and noisy-label memorization over training. Class-wise test curves do not establish this ordering.

record.verdict_notes: The extracted numerical values match Table 1. Symmetric corruption here always replaces a selected label with an incorrect class; the sweep stops at 80%. The original limits_scope verdict incorrectly treated an unmeasured component as an observed limitation. Additional table conditions are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labels, training error, and comparison with true-label training.
Relative training time and convergence speed as corruption increases.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training-set fit at each noise rate; the paper reports test accuracy but not whether training error remains zero.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevent fitting random labels, and whether removing them impairs true-label generalization.
The paper cites prior work on learning clean patterns before noisy labels, but does not test that ordering in its own experiments.

relationships.condition: Standard CE, 8-layer CNN, CIFAR-10, symmetric corruption rates 0–0.8
relationships.reason: R1–R5 show test accuracy decreasing monotonically from 89.26% to 34.80%, supporting the degradation component over the tested range; training fit is untested.
relationships.display_finding: Test accuracy declined monotonically from 89.26% to 34.80% across the corruption sweep.
